claims.text: Equiatomic FeCoNi is predominantly single-phase FCC and exhibits high saturation magnetization and low coercivity.
The intervention is to substitute part of equiatomic FeCoNi with Al to produce equiatomic FeCoNiAl.
Equiatomic FeCoNiAl satisfies the stipulated configurational-entropy threshold of at least 1.0R.
Adding an equiatomic amount of Al to FeCoNi will induce a multiphase microstructure.
FeCoNiAl will contain nanoscale B2-like ordered precipitates.
The B2-ordered precipitates will be fine, coherent, and dispersed in an FCC matrix.
Al addition locally reduces configurational entropy and promotes phase separation.
B2-like precipitates create heterogeneities in magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
The precipitate-induced anisotropy heterogeneities impede domain-wall motion through domain-wall pinning.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning increases the coercive field.
Equiatomic FeCoNiAl will have greater coercivity than soft FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt alloys.
The increased coercivity will be accompanied by saturation magnetization similar to that of the baseline alloys.
FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt are predominantly single-phase FCC alloys with soft-ferromagnetic behavior and low coercivity.
Arc melting, homogenization, and subsequent thermal treatment can produce or promote coherent nanoscale B2-like precipitates in FeCoNiAl.
Very high temperatures may dissolve the precipitates, and overaging may move the alloy outside the regime in which the hypothesis applies.
The volume fraction, size distribution, and coherency of the precipitates affect the magnitude of coercivity enhancement.
TEM and XRD will be used to test for nanoscale B2-like ordered precipitates, while VSM or SQUID measurements will determine coercivity and saturation magnetization.
The comparison should use a FeCoNiPt or similar soft FeCoNi-based alloy processed under comparable conditions.

The hypothesis is falsified if FeCoNiAl lacks a statistically significant coercivity increase beyond experimental error relative to the baseline, or if the expected coherent nanoscale precipitates are absent.
